dish: Pho, house noodle soup and beef massaman curry
w: Two-decade family kitchen in a York strip mall cooking Thai, Laotian and Vietnamese food — one of only three Pennsylvania restaurants on USA Today's 2024 Restaurants of the Year list.

dish: Made-from-scratch pasta (short-rib gnocchi) and the upstairs speakeasy tapas bar
w: Downtown York's Old-World Italian dining room — house-made pasta, soups and sauces, a Wine Spectator Award of Excellence (2025) and a speakeasy tapas bar upstairs.

dish: Whoopie pies from the on-site bakery (top of LNP's county taste test) and the Grand Smorgasbord
w: Strasburg-area PA Dutch smorgasbord and bakery, home of Lancaster's Whoopie Pie Festival; its whoopie pies topped LNP's blind taste test of county favorites.

dish: House meatballs, lasagna and the upside-down pizza
w: Hershey's oldest free-standing restaurant (since 1935) and the first in town to serve pizza (1947) — old family sauce recipes on Chocolate Avenue.

dish: Burgers, Reubens and chocolate desserts
w: Unpretentious, broad-menu grill in downtown Hershey that a local guide and the visitor bureau both send people to — burgers to lobster, with chocolate desserts to finish.

dish: Banana & Nutella crepe, French macarons and handmade European chocolates
w: Downtown Carlisle crêperie-chocolatier with super-sized crepes, house gelato and handmade chocolates, profiled behind the scenes by PA Eats.

dish: Barrel-aged and one-off beers from 100-ish taps, with pies from Al's of Hampden
w: West Shore brewery grown out of Al's of Hampden pizza shop — industrial setting, but routinely named the region's best beer, with around 100 drafts.

dish: Joose juicy IPA and Dark Necessity imperial stout
w: Camp Hill warehouse brewery (2016) known for hazy IPAs and stouts, board games and a window into the kitchen next door.

dish: Seasonal small plates — seared scallops with summer corn, the 25-layer zucchini–goat ricotta crêpe cake
w: French-inspired New American spot (opened 2024) cooking the county's farm bounty; named to the New York Times' 50 favorite restaurants in America and Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list.

dish: Arepas and Peruvian–Venezuelan plates
w: Food truck turned downtown restaurant (2025) — Lancaster County Magazine's #1 food truck, then #1 new restaurant, and on Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list.

dish: Spring rolls, banh mi and house French macarons
w: Third-generation Vietnamese family kitchen on Lititz Pike — spring rolls, banh mi and homemade desserts; on Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list.

dish: Wood-fired pizza
w: Casual wood-fired pizza offshoot of James Beard-nominated LUCA — #2 pizza in Lancaster County Magazine's Best of Lancaster 2025 and on Craig LaBan's 2026 list.

dish: Fine dining downstairs, rooftop patio and piano bar
w: Victorian-mansion dining room voted #1 dinner restaurant in Lancaster County Magazine's Best of Lancaster 2025; on OpenTable's Top 100 romantic restaurants.

dish: Nepalese momos and curries
w: Tiny downtown Nepalese–Indian locals' favourite (reserve — few tables), reviewed by LNP's IncognEATo.

dish: House-roasted espresso (Best Espresso in America contest winner, 2018)
w: Harrisburg's home-grown roaster (2010, founded by a rock drummer) — Uptown flagship plus downtown State St and Strawberry Square outposts; its barista won a national best-espresso contest.

dish: Small-batch roasts sweetened only with natural sweeteners and spices
w: Andrea Grove-Musselman's roaster, born at the Broad Street Market in 2014, now a café in a renovated Capitol-district building (and back at the market after the 2023 fire).

dish: Homemade ice cream — chocolate peanut butter soft-serve sundae, butter pecan, root beer floats
w: Sixteen flavours made on the premises in the 1819 Twin Sycamores House on Baltimore Street — the town's classic after-battlefield scoop.

dish: Shepherd's pie, bangers and mash and the Ulster fry
w: Gettysburg's only Irish-owned pub — trad music sessions and Irish home cooking a block off Lincoln Square.

dish: All-day diner breakfast and the cake case
w: Old-school 1950s-style diner off Lincoln Square where tourists, Gettysburg College students and locals share the counter.

dish: Family-style fried chicken, baked ham, corn and apple crisp in the barn
w: A 160-year-old barn in the Adams County apple country west of Gettysburg serving made-from-scratch family-style farm dinners with a touch of PA Dutch.

dish: Pecan sticky buns, hand pies and café au lait
w: Small downtown bakery-café for old-fashioned hand pies and extra-gooey pecan sticky buns before the battlefield.

dish: Fresh-cut battlefield fries and messy sandwiches
w: Counter-service fry shop by the battlefield visitor strip, famous for its fresh-cut fries and burgers.

dish: Pennsylvania rye whiskey (Wine Enthusiast 94 — the highest-scoring PA whiskey)
w: Revival of Lancaster County rye distilling, founded 2016 with Dick Stoll, last distiller of the old Michter's plant; tasting room a block off Main Street, Lititz. On Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list.

dish: Signature curries with fusion twists and plated desserts
w: Self-taught chef's downtown York dining room — named to USA Today's Restaurants of the Year list, the York Daily Record's pick for York's best.

dish: Hard ciders, house beer and brick-oven pizza on the farm
w: Working farm south of York with a cidery, brewery and seasonal farm-sourced restaurant — brick-oven pizzas and house-made ice cream.

dish: Rotating farmhouse ales and stouts (650+ recipes since 2016)
w: Brewery-restaurant hidden on a back alley in York's Royal Square, run by the Barnes family; eclectic, ever-changing tap list.

dish: Farm-made ice cream from its own herd's milk (250 rotating flavours)
address: 90 Indian Rock Dam Rd, York, PA 17403
w: Century family dairy farm that bottles its own hormone-free milk and churns it into ice cream at the farm store — 30 flavours in the case at a time.

dish: Farm-sourced comfort food and house-made ice cream on the Susquehanna patio
w: Riverside restaurant in an old Wrightsville warehouse across from Columbia — 60–70% of ingredients from local farms, with a patio over the Susquehanna.

dish: Italian classics and seafood, or Saturday Victorian tea
w: Pellegrini family's restaurant in a restored brownstone mansion in Middletown, serving since 1970 — reviewed by WITF's Phantom Diner.

dish: European-inspired bistro plates and an Old World wine list
w: Midtown neighbourhood bistro in a repurposed 1910 Victorian home, with sidewalk tables on Second Street.

dish: Award-winning house brews with homemade pizzas
w: Lebanon Valley craft-beer favourite's Palmyra brewpub (2023) in the Leed's Corner building, between Hershey and Lebanon.
